summary: Many owners find it comfortable and well built, with strong edge support, and some report six to ten years without sagging. The most common problems are sagging or body impressions after a few years and a firm feel that causes back pain, especially for side sleepers. Many ended up returning it.

Owners are split, but the largest group describes sagging or body impressions, often within two to four years, along with back pain. Many also found it too firm, and a number of owners mention a lingering chemical or wool smell. Some others report several comfortable, cool years, and warranty claims were often disputed.

Owners' opinions vary widely by firmness. Many owners wake with back pain, and the medium and firm versions are often called too firm or slow to break in, while some say the foam softens and hammocks. Plenty of others call it their best bed and report it easing back pain, and a fair number returned it.

Most owners like the crisp, cool feel, and many report these sheets lasting years. The main downside is durability for some, with holes, rips or thinning within months to two years, and several say quality dropped on newer sets. A few found the fabric scratchy at first, though it softens with washing.

Many owners find it comfortable and cooler than foam, and several report two to five years without problems or relief of back pain. The main complaints are sagging or softening, and firmness that causes hip and back pain, with some units reportedly firmer than the store model. Suits those who want a firmer hybrid feel.

Most owners who keep it like it, especially the soft version, and many side sleepers report less hip and back pain. Complaints are that the soft feels like quicksand or too soft over time, plus back pain for some and heat for a few. Some needed weeks or months to adjust.

Most owners say these sheets are soft and last, with many reporting several years of use without holes. The main downsides are that a few sets tore early or felt thin or rough, and some say newer sets were not as good as earlier ones. A couple found the price high unless bought on sale.

Owners lean negative on durability. Many owners report holes, torn seams or fitted sheet corners within about a year, and some found the linen thin, pilling or stiff. Customer service was mixed on replacements. A smaller group says it lasted years and gets softer with washing.

Most owners are very happy with the original Purple, with many reporting six to ten years of comfortable, cool sleep and no sag. The main downside is sagging in the middle or where people lie, which some owners hit after two to six years, and warranty claims could take effort. Heavier owners often also like it.

Most owners find it comfortable, and several couples and heavier side sleepers love it. The main downside is heat, with some saying the cooling top does not help. Firmness is also hit or miss, with some finding it too firm and others too soft in the softer options.

Owners are mixed. Several owners are happy with the cooling and long-term durability, particularly in the firm version. The most common complaint is that it feels too firm and takes weeks or months to break in, and a few report back pain or hip and shoulder aches for side sleepers. Some cite sagging.

Most owners praise the cooling and comfort and several report two years or more without problems. Downsides are some leaks and early failures, app or automatic temperature scheduling frustrations, and the high price. Support is often described as helpful, and some mention mismatched older hubs causing weaker cooling.

Owners are split. Some call it comfortable and durable over several years, while others report firmness that causes shoulder and back pain, or the opposite problem of too soft. A few owners saw sagging or dips within one to two years, and some say it sleeps warm. Fit seems to depend on body weight.

Owners agree it cools very well, but reliability is the main concern, with leaks and units failing within one to two years the top complaint. Others cite poor WiFi and app problems, noise and a steep price. Some owners report years of trouble-free use, and support responses were mixed.

Owners' views are mixed. The most common complaint is that the medium hybrid feels very firm, sometimes like concrete, and can cause back pain. Several say it still sleeps warm despite the cooling claims, though a few find it cool. Those who stick with it often praise the support and comfort after a break-in.

Most owners love it and describe it as comfortable, cool and supportive, with some calling it worth the price and a few taking it travelling. The main downside is that some pillows went flat after one to three years. A few found it too puffy or unsuitable.

Owners praise the cooling, but leaks are the dominant complaint, often after one to three years, and a few woke up to a soaked mattress. Replacement out of warranty was described as costly. Support was often quick when under warranty, and a few have had it work for two years without a problem.

Most owners find it comfortable and supportive, with several heavier sleepers and side sleepers praising it. The main downside is sagging or deep dips, which some reported within two years, sometimes with back and hip pain. Firmness choice matters, and a few found it warm or only fair at the edges.

Most owners find this weighted blanket breathable and cool, and several hot sleepers say it is the only weighted option they can use in summer. Complaints are few, including an odd smell on arrival and some fabric quality changes or pilling. Better suited to warm sleepers than those who want a snug feel.

Many long-term owners say it held up well, with several reporting seven to ten years of comfortable sleep. The downsides are that some found it too firm or hot, and a few developed sagging or back pain after four or more years. Reviews lean positive for side sleepers and couples.

Many owners sleep well on the Pod 5 and report no problems after months of use. The recurring downsides are hardware failures such as leaks or a clicking hub, slow or unhelpful support, buggy software and a required subscription. Some noticed no real sleep improvement.

Owners are split sharply. Some owners say it ended their back pain and gave pressure relief, including a few heavier sleepers. Others, often side sleepers, found their hips sink and ended up with back, neck or hip pain. Several also say it sleeps hot despite the cooling layer.

Most owners find it comfortable and fully light-blocking, with a speaker that works for sleep and meditation. The main downside is durability: the Velcro strap or cups wear out within months to a couple of years, and replacements are hard to get. Bulky cups bother some side sleepers.

Most owners find it comfortable, plush yet supportive, and several say it sleeps cool. The main downside is that it runs softer than expected for some, with a few reporting back or hip pain and returning it. A couple added a topper for more softness.

Most owners find it comfortable once the strap and cups are adjusted, and several say it suits side sleepers and lasts for years. The main complaint is that for some side sleepers the firm eye cups press on the face and leave marks. A few report wear, peeling cups or unhelpful support.

Owners are mixed. Several owners say it stayed comfortable for years, and some heavier sleepers like the plush support. The most common complaint is firmness: many found it too firm, though a few found it softer than expected. Some report sagging after several years.

Many owners like the firm support, and the flippable design lets them pick a firmness side. The main downsides are sagging or hip sinkage over time, and some find the firm side too firm. A few say the foam sleeps warm and one found edge support weak.

Most owners love the separate settings for each side and the heating and cooling, which lets couples sleep differently. The downsides are the high price, with some calling the temperature features gimmicky, and a few who found it uncomfortable and returned it. Fan noise bothered one.

Many owners say it ends night sweats and works well for couples, with some units running for years. It blows room air rather than making cold air. Downsides include fan noise, a frustrating app and, for a few, direct airflow or disappointment that led to a return.

Most owners like being able to add or remove fill, and many find it supportive, comfortable and durable over years. The downsides are that the foam can clump or flatten over time for some, and one owner found the warranty response unhelpful.

Owners are split. Several owners say it is supportive, holds its shape for years and is the best pillow they found. The main complaint is neck pain or poor fit, especially for some side and back sleepers, and its weight and bouncy grid feel are off-putting to some.

Many owners report it holding up for many years and still feeling good. Downsides include sleeping hot, body impressions and back pain as it ages, and a few say newer units feel softer or different from earlier ones.

Many owners find it comfortable and supportive, with some reporting relief from back pain. The main complaint is sagging, sometimes within a year or two. Firmness is a gamble, as some found the firmer options too hard, and a few returned it.

Most owners find it breathable and cooling, with weight that sits evenly and stays put, and some report it holding up for years. Downsides are that washing and drying take effort, toes can catch in the loops, and one owner noticed a chemical smell after washing.

Owners' reviews are mixed. Several owners say it lasted years and a few found it solved back pain or sinking. The main downsides are back pain and body impressions or sagging over time, and it may take weeks to break in. Firmness feels different between owners.

Many owners found it too firm, especially lighter side sleepers, and several report back pain. Sagging and sleeping hot also come up, and some say it feels different from the store model. A few like it and call it comfortable, and several returned it.

Several owners find it comfortable and good for back pain, at least at first. The main downside is sagging or deep sinkage, often within months to a year. A few found it much firmer than expected and returned it.

Most owners find it comfortable, springy and firm with some give, and several are very happy after months or years. It can feel firmer than expected and take time to break in. A couple returned it, and one reported sagging after about a year.
Many owners say it holds up for years and stays comfortable. The main downsides are firmness and related back, hip or shoulder pain, and some say it sleeps hot. A few added a topper to soften it.

Most owners find it comfortable, and some say it sleeps cool and has held up for years. The main complaint is sagging or dips in the middle, sometimes within months, and a few report back or hip pain. It is also very heavy.

Owners' reviews are mixed. Some owners had it last for years and heavier sleepers like the support. The main complaint is back pain, along with it feeling too firm or, in newer units, softer than older ones. Some report wear after several years.

Owners lean negative. Complaints include quality problems such as uneven expansion or undersized mattresses, sagging and back pain, and some found it too firm or poor value. A few liked it for comfort, and support has sometimes been helpful but sometimes slow.

Most owners find it comfortable and fully light-blocking, including for side sleepers and with CPAP. The adjustable cups are a favorite feature. Downsides are a break-in period for stiff cups, a price some call steep, and Velcro that loosens over time.

Most owners praise the deep pockets and stretch that keep the sheets in place, and many say they last for years. The main downside is pilling for some, along with wrinkling and bunching on thinner mattresses.

Most owners find it comfortable, and several say it sleeps cool and has held up for a year or more. The main downsides are sagging for some and softness that caused pain for a few, especially on the soft option. A couple needed time to adjust.

Owners are split by purchase date. Older Casper Original Pillows held up for years and wash well, while several newer ones went flat and unsupportive, with neck pain for a couple of owners. A few also found it not worth the price.
Owners mostly find it comfortable, soft yet supportive, and several report years of good use. A few found it too soft, dipping under the midsection and causing back pain.
Owners who love the comfort and relief from aches are matched by others reporting sagging in the middle, showing up within weeks to a few years. Sagging is the most common complaint.

Owners, especially heavier sleepers, mostly like the firm support and say it holds up, though some needed weeks to adjust. A few found it too firm for side sleeping, and one reported sagging after three years.
Owners are split. Too firm is the most common complaint, and a couple of long-term owners mention a rubber smell. Several others still find it comfortable and cool after years.
Owners mostly report sagging, often within days or weeks, with back pain and trouble getting warranty help for a couple. One owner found it great after six years.
Owners find them comfortable and good at blocking noise, but several report an earbud failing within months and slow warranty replacements.
Owners mostly report it holding up for many years and sleeping comfortably. A couple found it too firm or sagging within a month and returned it, and some sag appeared after a few years.
Owners mostly find it comfortable, with several happy after months or years. A few found the firmer versions too firm for their hips or shoulders.
Owners are divided. Some get back relief and no sagging, but a few sleep hot, back or shoulder pain recurs, and several returned it.
Owners mostly find it comfortable and cool-sleeping, though a few call it too firm. Some report sagging after several years while others have none.
Owners mostly like it, with several happy for side sleeping and over years, though feel varies: one found it too soft and another too firm until adding a topper.
Owners often find it firm at first, needing weeks or a free topper to settle, and several ended up happy. A couple found it too soft later and returned it.
Owners mostly like it, especially heavier sleepers and those wanting back support, and several report it holding up for years. A couple found it far too firm.
Owners mostly find it comfortable and supportive with few pressure points, though a couple returned it over pain or heat, and one saw a dip after a year.
Owners mostly report problems: too soft and unsupportive, with sagging or back aches for several. One side sleeper has had no sagging after a year and a half.
Owners who sleep on their side mostly find it keeps neck pain away and holds its shape, but a couple say it is poor on the back.
Owners mostly say it is the only pillow that supports their neck, including side sleepers. One found it too hard after a formula change.
Owners, several of them heavier sleepers, mostly call it among the best mattresses they have had, though a couple report sagging.
Owners like the sunrise wake-up and sleep sounds, but several say it depends on an app that keeps failing and puts features behind a subscription.
Owners mostly find the putty plugs comfortable and effective for sleeping, but they need replacing regularly, about weekly for one, which adds up.
Owners disagree on feel, with some calling it very firm and others softer than expected. Several report it holding up well, including for heavier sleepers.
Owners mostly find it comfortable, especially side sleepers, and a few say it sleeps cool, though one found it hot.
Several owners find it comfortable, especially side sleepers, with the medium getting the most praise. A couple found a firmer version too hard or needed a topper.
Owners are mixed. Several report dips or sagging after a year or more, and some found it too hard, though one still has a firm one after nearly four years.
Several owners found it too soft, with sagging or weak edges within weeks to a year. A couple of heavier sleepers found it comfortable and supportive.
Owners find it soft and long-lasting, but several still sleep hot under it despite the cooling claims.
Several owners of the firm versions report back pain, some after a good first stretch, and one side sleeper found it too hard.
Owners mostly report it softening and sagging after three to six years, with lower back or hip pain. One says it is like new after five years.
Owners say it blocks less noise than expected, with snoring and voices still getting through, and several question the price. A couple found it worked loose for side sleeping.
Most owners are happy, saying the buds work reliably out of the case and make a cheaper stand-in for Ozlo buds.
